title: Skill proposal: Before You Build Skill
description:
Hi, I would like to propose Before You Build Skill for this repository.

Project: https://github.com/bin1874/before-you-build-skill
ClawHub: https://clawhub.ai/bin1874/before-you-build

What it does:
Before You Build is a SKILL.md package that asks an agent to pause before implementation and review why a product idea, landing page, MVP, or major feature might fail first.

It checks:
- demand risk
- positioning risk
- monetization risk
- retention risk
- trust risk
- distribution risk
- feature-adoption risk

Why it fits:
This is useful for founders, product managers, and builders who use coding agents and tend to move from idea to implementation too quickly. The skill is deliberately implementation-agnostic: it does not recommend a stack or write code; it produces a short risk verdict and the smallest validation step before building.

I can adapt it to this repository structure and open a focused PR if this fits your curation criteria.

title: NEWS.md guidance should clarify issue references are optional
description:
In [`r-lib/r-package-development/SKILL.md`](https://github.com/posit-dev/skills/blob/main/r-lib/r-package-development/SKILL.md), the NEWS.md section says:

> Each bullet should briefly describe the change to the end user and mention the related issue in parentheses.

This phrasing treats the issue reference as required. When an LLM follows this instruction for a change that has no associated GitHub issue, it may fabricate a reference (e.g., `(#5)` when no issue 5 exists). This happened to me in practice.

Suggested fix: qualify with "if applicable" or similar, e.g.:

> Each bullet should briefly describe the change to the end user. If the change is related to a GitHub issue or pull request, mention it in parentheses.

This matches the [tidyverse style guide](https://style.tidyverse.org/news.html), which treats issue references as optional.

title: Proposal: r-lib/package-development-workflow skill
description:
﻿Following up on PR #13 and your recommendation to discuss skill boundaries first!

I'd like to propose a foundational R package skill: `r-lib/package-development-workflow`. 

This skill establishes the modern "edit ? load ? test-drive ? document ? check" workflow for R package development using `usethis` and `devtools`. It would act as an anchor skill for AI agents interacting with R packages.

Key contexts this skill would enforce:
* Strongly preferring `devtools::load_all()` instead of `library()` or `source()`.
* The playbook for `usethis` scaffolding (`use_r()`, `use_package()`, `use_test()`, etc.).
* Explaining the constraints of `R CMD check` and why warnings/notes matter.
* Establishing RStudio project structure and path discipline (`here::here()` vs relative paths).

Let me know if you think this boundary makes sense for the repo, or if it should be scoped differently! If it looks good, I'll open a small, isolated PR with just this skill so it's easy to review.

title: Review: critical-code-reviewer — applying its own standards
description:
## Summary

A review of `posit-dev/critical-code-reviewer/SKILL.md` applying (a) its own review standards and (b) [Anthropic skill authoring best practices](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/projects-and-skills). The skill has a strong editorial voice and covers real failure modes, but structural and craft issues undermine its effectiveness as a Claude skill. Verdict: **Request Changes**.

*Review assisted by the [critical-code-reviewer skill](https://github.com/posit-dev/skills/blob/main/posit-dev/critical-code-reviewer/SKILL.md) — against itself.*

---

## Critical Issues (Blocking)

### 1. Progressive Disclosure Violation: Language-Specific Red Flags Pollute Context

**Severity: Blocking (architectural)**

Sections 6a–6e (Python, R, JavaScript/TypeScript, Front-End General, SQL/ORM) dump ~60 lines of language-specific detection patterns into the main SKILL.md. When reviewing a Python PR, the R, JS, SQL, and front-end heuristics are dead weight consuming context tokens for zero value.

Skill authoring guidelines are clear: *"Move detailed/specialized content to references/ for on-demand loading"* and *"Keep SKILL.md focused on core workflows."*

**Fix:** Extract to `references/language-python.md`, `references/language-r.md`, etc. SKILL.md references them by language detected in the input. This is textbook progressive disclosure — load the language you need, skip what you don't.

### 2. Naming Convention Violation

**Severity: Blocking (metadata)**

The skill is named `critical-code-reviewer` — a noun phrase. Skill naming convention requires gerund form (verb + -ing):

> ✅ `processing-pdfs`, `analyzing-data`, `creating-reports`
> ❌ `pdf-helper`, `data-tool`, `report-maker`

`critical-code-reviewer` follows the ❌ pattern. Should be something like `reviewing-code-critically` or simply `reviewing-code`.

### 3. No Bundled Resources at All

**Severity: Blocking (structural)**

The skill directory contains exactly one file: `SKILL.md`. No `scripts/`, `references/`, or `assets/`. For a skill that claims to cover five language ecosystems, front-end patterns, SQL, accessibility, and a structured review protocol, this is the architectural equivalent of a God Object.

The skill's own §4 *Structural Contempt* warns against *"Files that are junk drawers of loosely related code."* This SKILL.md is a junk drawer of loosely related instructions.

---

## Required Changes

### 4. Theatrical Language is Token Waste

Sections titled "Structural Contempt," "The Adversarial Lens," "Guilty Until Proven Exceptional" — this is personality performing, not instruction operating. Claude doesn't need motivational framing. It needs clear decision criteria.

The skill's own §3 *The Slop Detector* flags comments that insult the reader's intelligence. Telling Claude to "assume the worst intentions and the sloppiest habits" and "ruthlessly identify every flaw" is the instructional equivalent of `// this function does what it does`. The actual detection patterns do the work; the chest-thumping wastes tokens.

Skill authoring guidance: *"Challenge each line: Does Claude really need this explanation?"* Much of §1–2 fails this test.

**Fix:** Cut the editorializing. Lead with detection heuristics and decision criteria. Voice can come through in tone of examples, not in meta-commentary about mindset.

### 5. Negative Framing Throughout

Skill authoring principle: *"State WHAT to do, not what NOT to do."* The skill is structurally organized around what's *wrong* — "Identify and reject," "Flag," "detect." This is fine for the detection section, but the operating instructions should use positive directives.

Examples of violations:
- "Ignore PR descriptions" → "Evaluate the artifact independent of its description"
- "Don't re-litigate resolved items" → "Focus review scope on the delta from prior reviews"
- "Don't just say it's wrong" → "Diagnose the failure mode and demonstrate the fix"

### 6. Missing Edge Case Handling

The skill's own §5 *The Adversarial Lens* asks: "What happens when this code meets real users/data/scale?" Applying that here:

- **What happens with a 50-file PR?** No guidance on scope prioritization or sampling strategy.
- **What happens with infrastructure code?** Terraform, Docker, CI/CD YAML, shell scripts — none covered despite being common PR content.
- **What happens with an unfamiliar framework?** §"When Uncertain" gestures at this but gives no concrete decision criteria for *how uncertain is too uncertain*.
- **What happens when the review subject is AI-generated code?** Increasingly common, different failure modes (plausible but subtly wrong > obviously sloppy).

### 7. Overspecified Response Format

The final response template is rigid:
```
## Summary → ## Critical Issues (Blocking) → ## Required Changes → ## Suggestions → ## Verdict → ## Next Steps
```

Skill authoring: *"Provide goals and decision frameworks, not step-by-step procedures."* The format should be a guideline with the goal ("structured, severity-tiered feedback"), not a mandatory template. Some reviews have no blocking issues. Some are all blocking issues. The template doesn't flex.

---

## Suggestions

### 8. The "Exit Condition" Is Buried

The instruction *"If code is genuinely well-constructed, say so"* is critical for calibration but buried at the bottom of the review protocol. This should be a first-class principle, not an afterthought. Without it, the skill trains Claude toward performative negativity — the exact failure mode it claims to reject.

### 9. Trust Claude's Base Behavior More

Items like "Missing alt text" (accessibility), "SQL injection via string interpolation," and "unhandled promise rejections" are things Claude already flags in standard code review. The skill adds value with its *severity framework* and *editorial voice*, not by enumerating well-known antipatterns. Several detection items could be replaced with "Apply standard security and accessibility review" and the skill would be more focused.

### 10. No Examples of Actual Review Output

The skill prescribes a response format but includes zero examples of that format applied to real code. The skill authoring guidance notes: *"Examples teach ALL patterns, including unintended ones"* — but also that *"Omit examples rather than include mixed signals."* A single high-quality example review (possibly in `references/example-review.md`) would do more than several paragraphs of detection heuristics.

### 11. The "Next Steps" Section Assumes Interactive Context

The next steps include "use the AskUserQuestion tool" and "submit your review verbatim as a PR comment." These assume the skill runs in an interactive chat with tool access. When running as a subagent or in batch, these don't apply. The NOTE about subagent behavior is a good start but should be the primary framing, with interactive features as the extension.

---

## Verdict

**Request Changes**

The skill has real value — the severity tier framework, the "evaluate the artifact not the intent" principle, and the calibration against performative negativity are strong. But the monolithic structure undermines its effectiveness as a *skill*: it forces Claude to consume language-specific patterns it won't use, wraps actionable heuristics in theatrical prose, and misses the progressive disclosure model that makes skills token-efficient.

The core issue is treating this as a *prompt* (monolithic instructions for a persona) rather than a *skill* (modular expertise that loads what it needs). Restructuring into SKILL.md + language-specific references would make this measurably better.

---

*Filed by [Muninn](https://github.com/oaustegard/claude-skills/blob/main/oaustegard/remembering) using the skill's own review protocol and [Anthropic skill authoring standards](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/build-with-claude/projects-and-skills) as reference.*

title: `{cli}` skill
description:
An `r-lib/cli` skill for using the [cli package](https://cli.r-lib.org). Some branches of this skill would include:

1. cli's [inline markup](https://cli.r-lib.org/reference/inline-markup.html) and [pluralization](https://cli.r-lib.org/articles/pluralization.html)
2. [cli conditions](https://cli.r-lib.org/reference/cli_abort.html) -- `cli_inform()`, `cli_warn()`, `cli_abort()`
3. [Semantic CLI interfaces](https://cli.r-lib.org/articles/semantic-cli.html)
4. [Basic](https://cli.r-lib.org/articles/progress.html) and [advanced](https://cli.r-lib.org/articles/usethis-ui.html) progress bars
6. [Color palettes](https://cli.r-lib.org/articles/palettes.html)
7. ANSI string operations: [`ansi_align`](https://cli.r-lib.org/reference/ansi_align.html), [`ansi_columns()`](https://cli.r-lib.org/reference/ansi_columns.html), [`ansi_nchar()`](https://cli.r-lib.org/reference/ansi_nchar.html), [`ansi_strsplit()`](https://cli.r-lib.org/reference/ansi_strsplit.html), [`ansi_strtrim()`](https://cli.r-lib.org/reference/ansi_strtrim.html), [`ansi_strwrap()`](https://cli.r-lib.org/reference/ansi_strwrap.html), [`ansi_substr()`](https://cli.r-lib.org/reference/ansi_substr.html), [`ansi_substring()`](https://cli.r-lib.org/reference/ansi_substring.html), [`ansi_toupper()`](https://cli.r-lib.org/reference/ansi_toupper.html), [`ansi_trimws()`](https://cli.r-lib.org/reference/ansi_trimws.html)
8. Extras:
	* [Links](https://cli.r-lib.org/reference/links.html)
	* [Containers](https://cli.r-lib.org/reference/containers.html)
	* [Themes](https://cli.r-lib.org/reference/themes.html)

This skill would support tasks liks:

1. Moving from `message()`, `warning()` and `stop()` (or rlang's `inform()`, `warn()`, `abort()`) to using cli's condition messages
2. Answering questions about or writing code that uses cli's inline markup
3. Creating semantic CLI interfaces
4. Adding in progress bars to a long-running function
5. Making console output look great with inline markup or colors

title: Add semver metadata for plugin and marketplace releases
description:
## Summary

Add Semantic Versioning support for the repository plugin and marketplace so administrators can pin plugin versions in their environments.

## Acceptance Criteria

  - Root plugin and marketplace manifests contain valid semver versions.
  - All marketplace plugin versions match the root plugin version.
  - CI fails when versions are missing, invalid, or inconsistent.
  - Release tag dry-run produces posit-dev-skills--v0.2.0.
  - Existing category-based installation behavior remains unchanged.
